latest_implementation.implementation_summary: Modified DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.BuildCamera() (the sole method responsible for the Main Camera in the door prototype scene) to replace the perspective test camera with a fixed orthographic isometric camera. The camera now sets `Camera.orthographic = true` with an `orthographicSize` of 8, and uses a fixed transform (position (10,10,-10), rotation Euler(30,45,0)) — the classic 30/45 dimetric isometric angle consistent with the GDD's Diablo 1 / Ultima Online-inspired presentation and with Unity's conventional "Isometric Z as Y" tilemap authoring angle referenced in the GDD's Runtime Implementation section. No rotation-input or camera-follow component was added, so the camera transform stays hard-fixed by the scene builder and cannot rotate freely — matching the candidate's "fixed" requirement. No Tilemap authoring or sprite-sorting work was touched, per the candidate's explicit scope exclusion. The disposable primitive Floor/Walls/Door/Player test room was left untouched as the visual verification target, also per scope.
tests_added: Build_MainCamera_IsFixedOrthographicIsometric — asserts camera.orthographic is true, orthographicSize > 0, camera rotation matches the fixed 30/45/0 isometric angle (not the old perspective angle), and no Rotate/Orbit-named component is attached to the camera hierarchy.
Build_RunTwice_MainCameraStaysSingleAndFixed — asserts re-running the scene builder does not duplicate the Main Camera and it remains orthographic.

latest_evaluation.summary: The Fixed Isometric Camera and Projection Setup goal is correctly implemented in DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.BuildCamera(): the camera is switched to orthographic projection with a fixed 30/45/0 dimetric rotation and fixed position, no rotation-input or orbit component is introduced anywhere in the codebase, and the diff is scoped strictly to the camera plus its new test coverage — no Tilemap, sprite-sorting, spell, or enemy work was absorbed. All four contract criteria pass with concrete code evidence.

criteria_results.evidence: Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Editor/DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs:117 sets `camera.orthographic = true;` and line 118 sets `camera.orthographicSize = IsometricOrthographicSize;` (8f, defined line 25) inside BuildCamera(), replacing the previous perspective camera entirely — no perspective-only fields (fieldOfView) are set.

DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs:23-24 defines `IsometricCameraEulerAngles = (30,45,0)` (classic dimetric isometric angle) and `IsometricCameraOffset = (10,10,-10)`; BuildCamera() (lines 110-122) applies these as a hard-coded fixed transform (`cameraObject.transform.position = IsometricCameraOffset; cameraObject.transform.rotation = Quaternion.Euler(IsometricCameraEulerAngles);`), replacing the prior perspective test angle noted in the contract (0,8,-8)/(45,0,0). This is a static, code-authored fixed isometric framing, not a runtime-computed or player-adjustable one.

BuildCamera() only assigns a Camera and AudioListener component to the camera GameObject (lines 112-115) and sets a fixed transform once at scene-build time; no orbit/rotation/look controller is attached. A project-wide grep for `Camera|orthographic` across all .cs files under Assets/ returns matches only in DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs and its test file — no separate camera-control or input-rotation script exists. PlayerMovement.cs (Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scripts/PlayerMovement.cs) only reads WASD keys to move the CharacterController via `controller.Move(...)`; it never touches Camera or Transform.rotation of the camera. The new test `Build_MainCamera_IsFixedOrthographicIsometric` (DoorPrototypeSceneBuilderTests.cs:95-116) also asserts no attached component has 'Rotate' or 'Orbit' in its type name.

implementation_result.json's files_modified lists exactly DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs and DoorPrototypeSceneBuilderTests.cs. Reading the full scene builder file confirms BuildCamera() is the only method changed for this goal; BuildFloor()/BuildWalls()/BuildDoor()/BuildPlayer()/BuildUI() (primitive test-room and UI) are unchanged and still use disposable primitives — no Tilemap, sprite-sorting, spell, or enemy code was added, matching implementation_scope's 'Single behavior: correct fixed isometric camera setup only.'
